summary: One or two days to answer is seen as reasonable if the candidate has what they need.
realLife: A career guide says one to two days is fair when you already have the information, three to five days is standard with competing factors, and a week or more is likely too long unless another offer is pending.
sources: Duke University career blog, how to evaluate a job offer and ask for time: https://careerhub.students.duke.edu/blog/2024/11/01/how-to-evaluate-a-job-offer-and-ask-for-time-to-think-about-it/
inGame: Needs: an offer record with a deadline; the deadline slot can be filled by a short span on the employer's job-offer call. Scene: needs a producer for job-offer.

turns.summary: The employer wants an answer the same day.
pulledBy: a vacancy that must be filled now
turns.writesBack: The candidate feels pressed, may turn down the offer, and the tie to the employer cools.

turns.summary: The employer gives a full week, and the candidate uses it to weigh other leads.
pulledBy: a candidate with another job lead
a record of the pay figure
turns.writesBack: The candidate decides with more information, and the employer waits.

turns.summary: The employer extends the deadline when asked for a few more days.
turns.writesBack: A small favor is owed, and the tie to the hiring manager gets closer.
